name: Hieroglyph Register
desc: A wall of carved hieroglyphs: reed, owl, eye, ankh, water, feather, sun, mouth, basket and seated-figure signs are incised into toned stone register by register, each an emboss that catches a raking lamp so that as the light travels the whole wall of relief shimmers, light rims sliding across the sunk carving. A cartouche rings a royal name. When the wall is full a fresh face is dressed and cutting begins again. Warm limestone incision, polychrome painted plaster, dark granite, or glyphs picked out in gold light.

energy.doc: carving relief contrast and raking-light glow

scale.doc: glyph size -- larger signs, fewer per register (obvious change)

speed.doc: how fast glyphs carve in, the light rakes, and the wall renews

paint.doc: polychrome saturation / how vivid the painted fills read

hue.doc: stone tone for the default; other styles fix their own

style.doc: aesthetic: warm limestone incision / polychrome painted plaster / dark granite / glyphs in gold light

seed.doc: deterministic -- re-throws the signs, registers and stone toning
